issue.title: Unable to install pinned SHA when extension uses binary releases
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

When installing an extension using a pinned SHA, the gh CLI is unable to install from source for a commit when it has binary releases.

### Affected version

```
gh version 2.70.0 (2025-04-11)
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Install gh-notify with a commit sha, that will work because the extension has no releases:
```console
$ gh extension install meiji163/gh-notify --pin 556df2eecdc0f838244a012759da0b76bcfeb2e7
Cloning into '/Users/leighmcculloch/.local/share/gh/extensions/gh-notify'...
remote: Enumerating objects: 379, done.
remote: Counting objects: 100% (224/224), done.
remote: Compressing objects: 100% (113/113), done.
remote: Total 379 (delta 149), reused 146 (delta 105), pack-reused 155 (from 1)
Receiving objects: 100% (379/379), 121.24 KiB | 1.86 MiB/s, done.
Resolving deltas: 100% (181/181), done.
✓ Installed extension meiji163/gh-notify
✓ Pinned extension at 556df2eecdc0f838244a012759da0b76bcfeb2e7
```
Install gh-dash with a comit sha, that will fail because the extension has releases:
```console
$ gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash --pin 605b25ac07928bfc13cde36c312a506d5bb01779 # v4.14.0
X Could not find a release of dlvhdr/gh-dash for 605b25ac07928bfc13cde36c312a506d5bb01779
````

### Expected vs actual behavior

I expected all extensions to be installable with a pinned commit sha and for it to be a security best practice to pin extension installs to a commit sha so that the user is in complete control of what gets installed since

comments.author: BagToad
comments.body:
Drive by thoughts, but maybe there's room for improvement in our `gh extension install` help docs:

```
For remote repositories, the GitHub CLI first looks for the release artifacts assuming
that it's a binary extension i.e. prebuilt binaries provided as part of the release.
In the absence of a release, the repository itself is cloned assuming that it's a
script extension i.e. prebuilt executable or script exists on its root.
```

I'll open a small PR to communicate what I think could be improve

comments.author: leighmcculloch
comments.body:
The problem with the existing behaviour of using releases as a decision branch for binary vs source, is that any extension that exists without a release can work, up until it's tagged, then all existing SHA pins fail.

> * Would you expect `gh` to compile arbitrary SHAs at install time locally on your computer?

Yes, I think so, by running some common command.

comments.author: BagToad
comments.body:
Given we support precompiled extensions from any ecosystem that can create a binary like Go and Rust and anything else someone can use to create a binary, I don't think there is going to be a common command.

Even if we were able to mostly determine what commands to run to build any arbitrary extension, I think we open the door to dependency & versioning issues that come with the territory of compiling locally from source; I don't think this aligns with the plug and play experience that `gh` ext

comments.author: BagToad
comments.body: Closing because I don't see a path forward, per https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/10837#issuecomment-2819660781
